source: One pool unit: one item at a time in service, first come first served, so M/M/1: E(W) = (rho/mu)/(1 - rho), rho = 0.75, 1/mu = 90 s: 270 s; Adan and Resing, Queueing Systems (2015), section 4.3
M/M/1 E(Lq) = rho^2/(1 - rho) = 2.25, an item holding a server unit while it waits for the pool counting as waiting (spec 2 "Pool"); Adan and Resing, Queueing Systems (2015), section 4.3
One unit of two in service a fraction rho = 0.75 of the time: 0.75/2; a unit waiting for the pool is not busy (spec 2 "Pool")
The pool unit is held exactly while an item is in service: rho = lambda/mu = 90 s / 120 s = 0.75

Two pool units and two server units: M/M/2, E(W) = Pi_W/(1 - rho) x 1/(c mu), Erlang C Pi_W = 9/14, rho = 0.75, c = 2, 1/mu = 90 s: 810/7 s (1.9286 min); Adan and Resing, Queueing Systems (2015), equations (5.1) and (5.3)
Busy pool units over 2: lambda/(c mu) = (1/60)/(2/90) = 0.75
